greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen. Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
penitential:
Lord, you are our rock and our fortress; Lord, have mercy.
Christ, you are our deliverer and our shield; Christ, have mercy.
Lord, you notice the son of man and take thought of him; Lord, have mercy.
psalm_response: Blessed be the Lord, my Rock!
homily:
We often think of time as a relentless march—a ticking clock that measures out our days, our achievements, and eventually, our limits. We look at our calendars, our schedules, our to-do lists, and we feel the pressure of the 'appointed time.' In the first reading today, the author of Ecclesiastes gives voice to the rhythm of human existence. He speaks of a time to be born, a time to die, a time to weep, and a time to laugh. It is a beautiful, haunting list that acknowledges the seasons of our lives. But he adds something crucial: God has 'put the timeless into their hearts.'

Think about that for a moment. We are creatures of time, bound by the sunset and the sunrise, yet we carry within us a longing for the eternal. We feel the ache of the passing shadow, as the Psalm says, but we also feel the tug of something that never passes away. We are like travelers who know we are just passing through, yet we are constantly looking for a home that feels permanent. We see this in the simple, everyday ways we try to capture the world. We take photos of a sunset, we record the voice of a loved one, we hold onto a memory because we intuitively know that beauty is meant to last, even when the moment itself slips through our fingers.

Benjamin Vo understood this. He was a boy who lived with one foot in the world of the future and one foot in the eternal present. He had that brilliant, analytical mind—the one that could code games, navigate cloud infrastructure, and dream of 'con chim airlines'—but he also had the heart of a poet. He was a boy who looked at the horizon not just to see where it ended, but to see where it led. He was a student of the world, a traveler who left his footprints across the globe, always curious, always seeking, always connecting. He didn't just pass through life; he engaged with it. He looked at the world with a sense of wonder that is the hallmark of a soul that knows it is made for more than just the dust.

Alan and Thao, I know that for these past three months, the 'time to weep' has felt like the only season you have known. You look at the empty chair, you look at the photos—perhaps that one of Ben sitting on the wooden bench, his braces showing in a bright, wide smile, with little girls hugging him from behind—and you feel the weight of the silence. You wonder about the 'appointed time.' You wonder why the clock stopped when it did. But do not let the silence of the house deceive you into thinking that the story has ended. The 'timeless' that God placed in Ben’s heart is the very thing that connects him to you now. That love is not a memory; it is a living, breathing reality in the presence of God. It is the thread that keeps the tapestry of your family intact, even when the pattern seems broken to our limited human eyes.

Ryan, my dear brother, you know the rhythm of Ben’s heart better than anyone. You know the laughter, the shared secrets, the way he looked at you with that quiet, steady affection. When you feel the absence of his voice, remember that you are the one who carries his legacy into the future. You are the one who continues to dream, who continues to build, who continues to live for the both of you. When you feel the weight of the world, remember that you are not just a brother who is left behind; you are a brother who is walking forward with his heart inside your own. Keep being the boy who knows that love is stronger than time. Keep the wonder alive. That is how you honor him. That is how you live in the light.

In the Gospel today, Jesus asks his disciples, 'Who do you say that I am?' It is a question that cuts through the noise of the crowds, the opinions of the world, and the confusion of the moment. He is asking for an anchor. Peter answers, 'The Christ of God.' It is the only answer that holds. Jesus then speaks of his own suffering, his own death, and his own resurrection. He shows them that the path to glory goes through the valley of the shadow. He shows them that God’s 'appointed time' is not a trap, but a doorway. He is the One who has already walked the road of suffering and come out the other side into the light of the Resurrection. He is the One who is holding Benjamin now in that same light.

I want to speak to those of you who might be carrying a heavy, hidden stone of self-reproach. Maybe you find yourself replaying the past, wondering if you missed a sign, or if you could have done more. Please, hear this truth today: God does not send these seasons of sorrow as a punishment, and He does not hold you responsible for the mysteries of life that are beyond human control. You were the parents Benjamin needed. You were the family he loved. You did not miss anything. You are not being accused by God, and you must not accuse yourselves. Let that stone fall. You are free to grieve, you are free to miss him, but you are not required to carry the burden of 'what if.' That is a weight that belongs to the past, and Christ has already stepped into the future to welcome Benjamin home. You are loved without limit, and you are being held by the same hands that hold him.

There is a profound, healing truth in the Psalm we prayed: 'Blessed be the LORD, my rock, my mercy and my fortress.' When the world feels like a shifting shadow, when the 'time to mourn' feels like it will never yield to a 'time to dance,' lean on the Rock. Do not try to solve the mystery of time. Do not try to reconcile the 'why' with the 'when.' Just rest in the 'Who.' The 'Who' is Jesus, and He is the one who promised, 'I will not leave you orphans.' He is the one who is even now preparing a place for you, a place where the seasons of weeping are over, and where the joy of the reunion will be eternal.

Think of the 'Well of Love' in Vietnam, that clean, life-sustaining water flowing in Ben’s name. It is a perfect image of his life. It is not a closed system; it is a source of life that keeps giving. His kindness, his empathy—the way he offered his piggy bank to help his uncle, the way he loved his family—that love is still flowing. It is still quenching the thirst of the poor. It is still bringing hope to the weary. His life was a gift that continues to unfold. You are the stewards of that gift. Every act of kindness you do, every time you choose to love instead of despair, you are keeping his spirit alive and flowing into the world.

So, what do you carry out the door today? It is a simple thing, but a profound one. When the weight of the 'appointed time' feels too heavy, when the silence feels too loud, do not look for answers in the calendar. Look for the presence in the 'Who.' When you see a plane in the sky, when you see a bird in flight, when you feel a sudden, warm memory of his smile, whisper his name, and then whisper the name of Jesus. Let those two names be your anchor. You are a family of four, and you are being led, step by step, through the darkness and into the light. The reunion is certain. And in the meantime, keep walking in the presence of God, in the light of the living. He is there, he is waiting, and he is watching over you with that same sweet, gentle smile. You are not walking alone. You are walking toward the Banquet, where all the laborers are gathered, where all the tears are wiped away, and where the love you shared will bloom forever. Amen.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you, and may His face shine upon you and give you peace. In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
standing_petitions: For our beloved Ben and all who have gone before us, that they may rest forever in the radiant light of Christ.
For all who are grieving, that God may console their hearts, strengthen their spirits, and fill them with the hope of eternal life.

readings.label: Reading 1
Responsorial Psalm
readings.text:
R. (1) Blessed be the Lord, my Rock!
Blessed be the LORD, my rock,
my mercy and my fortress,
my stronghold, my deliverer,
My shield, in whom I trust.
R. Blessed be the Lord, my Rock!
LORD, what is man, that you notice him;
the son of man, that you take thought of him?
Man is like a breath;
his days, like a passing shadow.
R. Blessed be the Lord, my Rock!

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text:
Once when Jesus was praying in solitude,
and the disciples were with him,
he asked them, “Who do the crowds say that I am?”
They said in reply, “John the Baptist; others, Elijah;
still others, ‘One of the ancient prophets has arisen.’”
Then he said to them, “But who do you say that I am?”
Peter said in reply, “The Christ of God.”
He rebuked them and directed them not to tell this to anyone.

He said, “The Son of Man must suffer greatly
and be rejected by the elders, the chief priests, and the scribes,
and be killed and on the third day be raised.”

Hãy đi đến những nơi mà Ben muốn nha và đừng quên là luôn nhớ về gia đình mình nhé, thương em trai nhiều. Giá như !!!!!!!!!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: What happened my son? It's been 3 months since you left us. Missing you so much my whole body aches. Mom cries every day now... What are we going to do now Ben?  Please pray for us.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben,

Rafael Rizzo and his little brother Ben really need your help right now. Please bless them with good health and give them the strength to get through this together. Please watch over Brandon and Flor's health, too.

I miss you a whole bunch. I know you're up in heaven watching over all of us. Whenever you're able to, stop by to visit, yeah? I love you and miss you so much!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben - Miss you a whole bunch. Crying all day yesterday, i hope today will be better. Please guide our family through this grief... There's a 14 year old boy that just left earth on August 12... His name is Phero Aden Vo - look for him, maybe you guys can be friends...

Please pray for me and mom to have good health and strength.

I love and miss you Ben

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben, Trustin visited you today and left you a few airplane cards—we're putting them in your room for you. Please pray for Trustin and his family to stay healthy and strong. Be a guardian angel to Trustin and Ryan as they go through school, and help guide their steps through every year to come.

Ben ơi, Làm cả ngày tới tối, đến lúc chuẩn bị đi ngủ thì nằm một lúc lại nhớ Ben, nhớ mấy chuyện hai anh em từng nói với nhau. Nghĩ tới em, anh thấy buồn nhiều lắm. Ben hãy luôn theo dõi và cầu nguyện cho ba mẹ và Ryan nhé, nước mắt chảy ngược nó khủng khiếp hơn chảy xuôi đó Ben.

Ben ơi, ba nhớ con nhiều quá.

Mommy cũng vậy. Hơn hai tháng rồi mà ba má vẫn khóc mỗi ngày.

Con giúp ba má vượt qua nha, để lo cho em
Hey Ben,  nếu có thể hãy cho anh Minh gặp Ben trong giấc mơ nhé, dù chỉ là lời chào hay nụ cười như cách Ben vẫn hay tạo dáng để chụp hình. Nhớ và thương Ben nhiều lắm
